source.data: synthetic households (not survey data); see data/DATACARD.md

splash.title: Set up your home's privacy rules
splash.text: We'll show you up to 15 short situations, like a camera sending video to its maker. Tell us whether you'd allow each one. From your answers we set up rules for every smart device in your home, before any of them joins. It takes about three minutes, you can change any rule later, and you can redo this at any time.

follow_up_intro.title: Help us get the details right
follow_up_intro.text: Households like yours are split on these situations, so we'd rather ask than guess.

cell_usageData_communicationsAndNotifica.prompt: A device sends how you use your devices (for example, when you switch the lights on, or what you watch on TV) to the company that made it, to send you alerts and messages (for example, a doorbell or smoke alarm notification). Would you allow this?

data_examples.light_plug: how you use your devices (for example, when you switch your lights on and off)

data_examples.camera: how you use your devices (for example, when you check your camera from your phone)
data_examples.lock_entry: how you use your devices (for example, when you lock and unlock your door)

walk: Stage 1: show the root question; follow the branch whose 'answers' contain the chosen option; repeat until a node has 'preset'. A question can come back further down a path: reuse the earlier answer, never ask twice. Stage 2: ask the leaf's 'follow_ups' in order, at most 'follow_up_budget' of them (the cap minus the questions asked in stage 1). Skip any follow-up already answered in stage 1.
rules: Copy the preset's rules from presets.json. For every situation question answered 'yes' or 'no' (stage 1 or 2), where the rule covering that situation says otherwise, split that rule around the situation (at most three pieces: other data types; this data type with other purposes; this data type and purpose with other handling contexts) and add a rule with the answer for the situation itself ('yes' = allow, 'no' = never; origin kind 'answer'). 'Not sure' keeps the preset. Rules never overlap, so exactly one decides each flow.
rerun: Rerunning the questionnaire starts over: the household's rules are rebuilt from the new answers; manual edits are replaced after a warning.
